I'm going by the runbook, which never auto-fixes and gives a person for every row, so under rule 3 I'll decide right away that this goes to a person, quoting that row. Since a case for a person always ends with RaiseToPerson, I'll call that too, and I'll state the summary before the tool call. The ArgumentOutOfRange error isn't listed as an expected exception, so I won't ignore it. The order is DecideCase first, then RaiseToPerson.

I've settled on the person decision, so I'm checking whether the two calls can go in one block. They don't depend on each other, so I'll put DecideCase and RaiseToPerson together.

This is an unlisted exception, and the refund runbook never allows an automatic fix: every row of its Decisions table sends the case to payments. So I'm giving it to a person now, without investigating. The exception is `System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from `RefundOrder` (`Api/Refund.cs`, line 12), which moves money, so payments must check whether the customer was refunded.
